migrations.name: 0005_identity_providers.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Identity providers (OpenID Connect). Apply as a NEW numbered migration after
-- the accounts schema. Every statement is IF NOT EXISTS, so a store that applied
-- an earlier version of this file applies the current one again as its next
-- migration and gains only what it lacks.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_transactions (
  state_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  binding_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  config_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload TEXT NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_transactions_expiry ON oa_oidc_transactions(expires_at);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_limits (
  bucket TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  count INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
-- One pinned link per configured provider. Linking stores the issuer, JWKS URI,
-- client id, endpoints and allowed algorithms; a changed configuration only
-- records a pending re-link, which the owner completes with a step-up proof.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_identity_providers (
  provider_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  preset TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('linked','unlinked')),
  issuer TEXT NOT NULL,
  client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  jwks_uri TEXT NOT NULL,
  authorization_endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
  algorithms TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_auth_method TEXT NOT NULL,
  response_iss INTEGER NOT NULL,
  interface_version TEXT,
  linked_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  pending_issuer TEXT,
  pending_client_id TEXT,
  pending_preset TEXT,
  pending_at INTEGER,
  jwks TEXT,
  jwks_fetched_at INTEGER
);
-- Reachability per configured provider, linked or not. A provider that has
-- failed discovery or JWKS for 5 minutes, or answered 404 or a DNS failure, is
-- hidden from the sign-in page until a later check succeeds.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_identity_provider_health (
  provider_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  failing_since INTEGER,
  hard_failure_at INTEGER,
  checked_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

migrations.sql:
-- Gasket: one site, its people and roles, the asset register, parts, checklists,
-- schedules, work orders and their evidence, reviews, agent proposals and audit.
-- Append-only history is enforced here by triggers, not only by the handlers.

CREATE TABLE gk_site (
  singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (singleton = 1),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  timezone TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- A person with access. The owner is the Base operator with role 'owner'.
CREATE TABLE gk_members (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('owner', 'lead', 'maintainer', 'supervisor', 'agent')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active', 'ended')),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE gk_assets (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  tag TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  serial TEXT,
  location TEXT NOT NULL,
  custodian TEXT,
  category TEXT,
  criticality TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' CHECK (criticality IN ('normal', 'important', 'critical')),
  notes TEXT,
  retired_at INTEGER,
  origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'native' CHECK (origin IN ('native', 'import')),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  import_revision TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- import_revision holds the import kit's applied revision for rows a move-in created.

-- Every earlier version of an asset's identity, written on each edit.
CREATE TABLE gk_asset_versions (
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL,
  value_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  changed_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  changed_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (asset_id, revision)
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_asset_versions_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_asset_versions BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

-- A physical sighting of an asset, to reconcile the register against the floor.
CREATE TABLE gk_sightings (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  outcome TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN ('found', 'elsewhere', 'missing')),
  seen_location TEXT,
  note TEXT,
  recorded_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_sightings_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_sightings BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_meters (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  unit TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('counter', 'gauge', 'condition')),
  origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'native' CHECK (origin IN ('native', 'import')),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  import_revision TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (asset_id, name)
);

-- Readings are dated by when the person took them (taken_on, local date and time).
CREATE TABLE gk_readings (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  meter_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_meters(id),
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  work_order_id TEXT,
  value TEXT NOT NULL,
  taken_on TEXT NOT NULL,
  entered_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  entered_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'native' CHECK (origin IN ('native', 'import')),
  import_revision TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX gk_readings_meter ON gk_readings(meter_id, taken_on);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_readings_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_readings BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER gk_readings_native_keep BEFORE DELETE ON gk_readings WHEN OLD.origin <> 'import' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_parts (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  number TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  unit TEXT NOT NULL,
  minimum_milli INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (minimum_milli >= 0),
  location TEXT,
  origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'native' CHECK (origin IN ('native', 'import')),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  import_revision TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- Quantities in thousandths of the part's unit. On-hand is the sum of movements.
CREATE TABLE gk_part_moves (
  seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_parts(id),
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('opening', 'receive', 'issue', 'return', 'count')),
  quantity_milli INTEGER NOT NULL,
  counted_milli INTEGER,
  work_order_id TEXT,
  note TEXT,
  actor TEXT NOT NULL,
  at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'native' CHECK (origin IN ('native', 'import'))
);
CREATE INDEX gk_part_moves_part ON gk_part_moves(part_id, seq);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_part_moves_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_part_moves BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER gk_part_moves_native_keep BEFORE DELETE ON gk_part_moves WHEN OLD.origin <> 'import' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_checklists (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- A published revision never changes; work orders point at the revision they used.
CREATE TABLE gk_checklist_revisions (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  checklist_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_checklists(id),
  number INTEGER NOT NULL,
  items_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  note TEXT,
  published_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  published_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (checklist_id, number)
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_checklist_revisions_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_checklist_revisions BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_schedules (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  checklist_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_checklists(id),
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  every_days INTEGER CHECK (every_days IS NULL OR every_days BETWEEN 1 AND 3660),
  meter_id TEXT REFERENCES gk_meters(id),
  every_units TEXT,
  next_due_date TEXT,
  next_due_meter TEXT,
  assignee_id TEXT REFERENCES gk_members(id),
  active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK (every_days IS NOT NULL OR meter_id IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE gk_work_orders (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  number INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('preventive', 'corrective')),
  schedule_id TEXT REFERENCES gk_schedules(id),
  follow_up_of TEXT,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  checklist_revision_id TEXT REFERENCES gk_checklist_revisions(id),
  due_date TEXT NOT NULL,
  due_meter TEXT,
  assignee_id TEXT REFERENCES gk_members(id),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('open', 'in_progress', 'submitted', 'returned', 'closed', 'cancelled')),
  version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  submitted_at INTEGER,
  closed_at INTEGER,
  closed_by TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX gk_work_orders_asset ON gk_work_orders(asset_id, due_date);
-- One open work order per schedule.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX gk_work_orders_one_open ON gk_work_orders(schedule_id) WHERE schedule_id IS NOT NULL AND status NOT IN ('closed', 'cancelled');

-- The latest result per checklist item; the handler also appends every result to gk_result_log.
CREATE TABLE gk_results (
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  item INTEGER NOT NULL,
  outcome TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN ('pass', 'fail', 'attention')),
  note TEXT,
  recorded_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (work_order_id, item)
);
CREATE TABLE gk_result_log (
  seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  item INTEGER NOT NULL,
  outcome TEXT NOT NULL,
  note TEXT,
  recorded_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_result_log_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_result_log BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_evidence (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  filename TEXT NOT NULL,
  media_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  size INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
  bytes BLOB NOT NULL,
  uploaded_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  uploaded_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_evidence_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_evidence BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

-- Times are local site date-times (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM); minutes are computed when it ends.
CREATE TABLE gk_downtime (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  work_order_id TEXT REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  started_on TEXT NOT NULL,
  ended_on TEXT,
  minutes INTEGER,
  reason TEXT NOT NULL,
  recorded_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX gk_downtime_one_open ON gk_downtime(asset_id) WHERE ended_on IS NULL;
CREATE TRIGGER gk_downtime_end_once BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_downtime WHEN OLD.ended_on IS NOT NULL BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_findings (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  severity TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (severity IN ('low', 'medium', 'high')),
  text TEXT NOT NULL,
  follow_up_id TEXT,
  recorded_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_findings_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_findings BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_reviews (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  version INTEGER NOT NULL,
  decision TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (decision IN ('approved', 'returned')),
  reason TEXT,
  reviewer TEXT NOT NULL,
  at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_reviews_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_reviews BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

-- Agent-prepared proposals. Approval records the exact payload hash it ran.
CREATE TABLE gk_proposals (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('schedule', 'corrective', 'count')),
  payload_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  basis_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  reasoning TEXT NOT NULL,
  prepared_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  prepared_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected')),
  decided_by TEXT,
  decided_at INTEGER,
  decision_note TEXT,
  result_id TEXT
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_proposals_decide_once BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_proposals WHEN OLD.status <> 'pending' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_audit (
  seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  actor TEXT NOT NULL,
  action TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject TEXT NOT NULL,
  detail TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_audit_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_audit BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER gk_audit_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON gk_audit BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

-- In-batch preconditions: a row with ok <> 1 aborts the whole batch with its code.
CREATE TABLE gk_guard (code TEXT NOT NULL, ok INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_guard_stale BEFORE INSERT ON gk_guard WHEN NEW.ok IS NOT 1 AND NEW.code = 'stale' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_guard_stale'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER gk_guard_stock BEFORE INSERT ON gk_guard WHEN NEW.ok IS NOT 1 AND NEW.code = 'insufficient_stock' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_guard_insufficient_stock'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER gk_guard_return BEFORE INSERT ON gk_guard WHEN NEW.ok IS NOT 1 AND NEW.code = 'return_exceeds_issue' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_guard_return_exceeds_issue'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER gk_guard_other BEFORE INSERT ON gk_guard WHEN NEW.ok IS NOT 1 AND NEW.code NOT IN ('stale', 'insufficient_stock', 'return_exceeds_issue') BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_guard_failed'); END;

-- MIG-002 (slice): completed MaintainX work orders moved in as asset history.
-- A history row keeps its MaintainX ID, type, completion time and who completed
-- it, categories, recurrence and costs (whole cents). It is history only: it

CREATE TABLE gk_work_history (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  source_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('preventive', 'corrective', 'other')),
  description TEXT,
  completed_on TEXT NOT NULL,
  completed_by TEXT,
  assigned_to TEXT,
  categories TEXT,
  recurrence TEXT,
  parts_cents INTEGER,
  labor_cents INTEGER,
  other_cents INTEGER,
  origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'import' CHECK (origin = 'import'),
  import_revision TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX gk_work_history_asset ON gk_work_history(asset_id, completed_on);

migrations.name: 0025_codes.sql
migrations.sql:
-- ASSET-004: one central, ordered catalog of criticality levels and risk,
-- failure mode, cause and remedy codes. Leads add, reorder, relabel and retire
-- codes; a code's key never changes, records keep the code they were given and
-- retired codes stay readable. Import names map an imported value onto a code.
CREATE TABLE gk_codes (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('criticality', 'risk', 'failure_mode', 'cause', 'remedy')),
  key TEXT NOT NULL,
  label TEXT NOT NULL,
  import_names TEXT,
  position INTEGER NOT NULL,
  retired_at INTEGER,
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (kind, key)
);
INSERT INTO gk_codes (id, kind, key, label, position, created_at) VALUES
  ('criticality:normal', 'criticality', 'normal', 'Normal', 1, 0),
  ('criticality:important', 'criticality', 'important', 'Important', 2, 0),
  ('criticality:critical', 'criticality', 'critical', 'Critical', 3, 0);

-- Asset criticality is a catalog level now, not a fixed list: rebuild gk_assets without its CHECK.
PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = true;
CREATE TABLE gk_assets_next (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  tag TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  serial TEXT,
  location TEXT NOT NULL,
  custodian TEXT,
  category TEXT,
  criticality TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal',
  notes TEXT,
  retired_at INTEGER,
  origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'native' CHECK (origin IN ('native', 'import')),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  import_revision TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO gk_assets_next (id, tag, name, serial, location, custodian, category, criticality, notes, retired_at, origin, revision, import_revision, created_at, updated_at)
  SELECT id, tag, name, serial, location, custodian, category, criticality, notes, retired_at, origin, revision, import_revision, created_at, updated_at FROM gk_assets;
DROP TABLE gk_assets;
ALTER TABLE gk_assets_next RENAME TO gk_assets;

-- Findings carry codes (each optional); moved-in work history carries the failure mode its category mapped to.
ALTER TABLE gk_findings ADD COLUMN failure_mode TEXT REFERENCES gk_codes(id);
ALTER TABLE gk_findings ADD COLUMN cause TEXT REFERENCES gk_codes(id);
ALTER TABLE gk_findings ADD COLUMN remedy TEXT REFERENCES gk_codes(id);
ALTER TABLE gk_findings ADD COLUMN risk TEXT REFERENCES gk_codes(id);
ALTER TABLE gk_work_history ADD COLUMN failure_mode TEXT REFERENCES gk_codes(id);

-- PM-006: chasing overdue work. The site's chase rule (appended revisions),
-- in-app notices (one per recipient and occasion), the assignee's responses,
-- blockers with an owner, next action and promised date, and the day a work
-- order first became overdue, which no reassignment or reschedule resets.
CREATE TABLE gk_chase_rules (
  number INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  remind_before_days INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (remind_before_days BETWEEN 0 AND 30),
  response_within_days INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (response_within_days BETWEEN 0 AND 30),
  lead_after_days INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (lead_after_days BETWEEN 0 AND 90),
  supervisor_after_days INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (supervisor_after_days BETWEEN 0 AND 180),
  approved_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  approved_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE gk_notices (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  recipient_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('reminder', 'overdue', 'escalation_lead', 'escalation_supervisor', 'blocker_missed')),
  occasion TEXT NOT NULL,
  text TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (recipient_id, occasion)
);
CREATE INDEX gk_notices_recipient ON gk_notices(recipient_id, created_at);

CREATE TABLE gk_chase_responses (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  response TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (response IN ('on_it', 'blocked')),
  note TEXT,
  member_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE gk_blockers (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('parts', 'access', 'skill', 'production')),
  owner_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  next_action TEXT NOT NULL,
  promised_on TEXT NOT NULL,
  raised_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  raised_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  resolved_at INTEGER,
  resolved_by TEXT,
  resolution TEXT
);
ALTER TABLE gk_work_orders ADD COLUMN overdue_since TEXT;

migrations.sql:
-- PART-002: parts reservations, repair kits and approved substitutes. A lead
-- approves one part as a substitute for another (one direction) and keeps
-- repair kits (fixed lines of parts and quantities). A planner reserves a part,
-- or a kit's lines, to open work; a work order holds at most one open
-- reservation per part. A reservation ends when a planner releases it or its

migrations.name: 0038_comments.sql
migrations.sql:
-- PLAN-006: comments, mentions and shift handoff on work orders and assets.

-- sequence (the order threads list in and unread state counts by). Every
-- version of its text is a kept revision; photos keep their bytes and digest;
-- mentions give the person an in-app notice that links to the comment, so
-- gk_notices takes asset and comment links and a new kind. Each person's read
-- marker per record is the highest comment sequence they have read there.
CREATE TABLE gk_comments (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

);
CREATE INDEX gk_comments_work ON gk_comments(work_order_id, seq);
CREATE INDEX gk_comments_asset ON gk_comments(asset_id, seq);

CREATE TABLE gk_comment_revisions (
  comment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_comments(id),

  body TEXT NOT NULL,
  edited_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  edited_at INTEGER NOT NULL,

);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_comment_revisions_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_comment_revisions BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_comment_mentions (
  comment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_comments(id),
  member_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_members(id),

CREATE TABLE gk_comment_photos (

CREATE TRIGGER gk_comment_photos_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_comment_photos BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_comment_reads (
  member_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_members(id),
  subject_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (subject_kind IN ('work', 'asset')),
  subject_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  read_seq INTEGER NOT NULL,

);

migrations.name: 0043_location_work.sql

PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = true;
CREATE TABLE gk_work_orders_keep AS SELECT * FROM gk_work_orders;
CREATE TABLE gk_work_orders_next (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

ALTER TABLE gk_work_orders_next RENAME TO gk_work_orders;
INSERT INTO gk_work_orders (id, number, asset_id, kind, schedule_id, follow_up_of, title, description, checklist_revision_id, due_date, due_meter, assignee_id, status, version, created_by, created_at, submitted_at, closed_at, closed_by, merged_into, acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by, trigger_reading_id, occurrence, overdue_since, team_id, trade, shift, estimate_minutes, priority, template_id, template_revision)
  SELECT id, number, asset_id, kind, schedule_id, follow_up_of, title, description, checklist_revision_id, due_date, due_meter, assignee_id, status, version, created_by, created_at, submitted_at, closed_at, closed_by, merged_into, acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by, trigger_reading_id, occurrence, overdue_since, team_id, trade, shift, estimate_minutes, priority, template_id, template_revision FROM gk_work_orders_keep ORDER BY number;

);
INSERT INTO gk_findings_next (id, work_order_id, asset_id, severity, text, follow_up_id, recorded_by, recorded_at, item, rule_id, failure_mode, cause, remedy, risk)

DROP TABLE gk_findings;

-- ASSET-007: an asset's lifecycle facts (purchase, commissioning, warranty,

CREATE TABLE gk_asset_lifecycle (

migrations.name: 0048_typed_steps.sql

migrations.sql:
-- FIELD-005: before/after photos, annotations and signatures. Evidence keeps
-- its phase (before or after the work), when it was taken (site local time),
-- the door it came through and, for PNG and JPEG, its pixel size. An
-- annotation is a shape over a photo in hundredths of a percent of its width
-- and height, with a note; the original file is never changed. A signature is
-- bound to the work order's version when it was given; a change to the work
-- makes it stale and submission waits until it is given again.
ALTER TABLE gk_evidence ADD COLUMN phase TEXT CHECK (phase IS NULL OR phase IN ('before', 'after'));
ALTER TABLE gk_evidence ADD COLUMN taken_on TEXT;
ALTER TABLE gk_evidence ADD COLUMN door TEXT;
ALTER TABLE gk_evidence ADD COLUMN width INTEGER;
ALTER TABLE gk_evidence ADD COLUMN height INTEGER;
ALTER TABLE gk_work_orders ADD COLUMN submitted_version INTEGER;
CREATE TABLE gk_annotations (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  evidence_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_evidence(id),
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  shape TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (shape IN ('box', 'ellipse', 'arrow')),
  x1 INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (x1 BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
  y1 INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (y1 BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
  x2 INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (x2 BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
  y2 INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (y2 BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
  note TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_annotations_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_annotations BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;
CREATE TABLE gk_signatures (

  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),

  mark BLOB,
  mark_sha256 TEXT,
  door TEXT NOT NULL,
  recorded_by TEXT NOT NULL,

);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_signatures_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_signatures BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

migrations.name: 0052_asset_documents.sql
migrations.sql:
-- ASSET-003: an asset's documents (OEM manuals, diagrams, warranties,
-- authorizations such as permits, licences and certificates, and others), each
-- a series of numbered revisions that never change, with the publisher and
-- reference the file came from. A document may expire: its named owner gets an
-- in-app notice when it is within its reminder days and again when it has
-- expired. Work pins the revision it was given, so a later revision of the
-- master never changes what issued work shows or packs. Supplier and service
-- contacts sit on the asset; commissioning stays in gk_asset_lifecycle.
CREATE TABLE gk_documents (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

  expires_on TEXT,
  owner_id TEXT REFERENCES gk_members(id),
  remind_days INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CHECK (remind_days BETWEEN 0 AND 365),
  created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK (expires_on IS NULL OR owner_id IS NOT NULL)
);
CREATE INDEX gk_documents_asset ON gk_documents(asset_id, kind, title);
CREATE INDEX gk_documents_expiry ON gk_documents(expires_on) WHERE expires_on IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE gk_document_revisions (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  document_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_documents(id),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL,
  filename TEXT NOT NULL,
  media_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  size INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
  bytes BLOB NOT NULL,
  source TEXT NOT NULL,
  note TEXT,
  added_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  added_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (document_id, revision)
);
CREATE TRIGGER gk_document_revisions_keep BEFORE UPDATE ON gk_document_revisions BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER gk_document_revisions_stay BEFORE DELETE ON gk_document_revisions BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'gasket_immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE gk_work_documents (
  work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_work_orders(id),
  document_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_documents(id),
  revision_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_document_revisions(id),
  linked_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  linked_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (work_order_id, document_id)
);

CREATE TABLE gk_asset_contacts (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_assets(id),
  role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('supplier', 'manufacturer', 'service', 'other')),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  company TEXT,
  phone TEXT,
  email TEXT,
  recorded_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX gk_asset_contacts_asset ON gk_asset_contacts(asset_id, role, name);

CREATE TABLE gk_notices_next (

  occasion TEXT NOT NULL,

);
INSERT INTO gk_notices_next (id, recipient_id, work_order_id, asset_id, comment_id, kind, occasion, text, created_at) SELECT id, recipient_id, work_order_id, asset_id, comment_id, kind, occasion, text, created_at FROM gk_notices;

migrations.name: 0053_part_valuation.sql
0054_cycle_counts.sql
migrations.sql:
-- PART-004: planned blind cycle counts. A lead or the owner plans a count of
-- one shelf location (or chosen parts) for one counter; the count sheet never
-- shows its counter the expected quantity. Each line keeps the on-hand and
-- movement sequence at the moment the count was submitted, so movements during
-- and after the count reconcile instead of being undone: an approved variance
-- posts counted minus that expected quantity. Variances valued at or above

CREATE TABLE gk_counts (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  number INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  location TEXT,
  counter_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_members(id),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open', 'submitted')),
  planned_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  planned_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  submitted_at INTEGER
);

  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  count_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gk_counts(id),

  counted_milli INTEGER,
  expected_milli INTEGER,
  seen_seq INTEGER,
  reason TEXT CHECK (reason IS NULL OR reason IN ('lost', 'found', 'damaged')),
  note TEXT,
  state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (state IN ('open', 'matched', 'posted', 'waiting', 'approved', 'rejected')),
  move_id TEXT,
  decided_by TEXT,
  decided_at INTEGER,
  decision_note TEXT,
  UNIQUE (count_id, part_id),

);
CREATE INDEX gk_count_lines_part ON gk_count_lines(part_id);
